lesson.title: When to Go Down the Line
lesson.hook: The line isn't much riskier than crosscourt. What makes it right or wrong is where they are.
lesson.memHTML: Line when they're off it. Crosscourt when they're on it.
lesson.tomorrow: Before you change direction, check where they are: still recovering, go line; already covering it, go crosscourt.

drill.name: Line or cross
drill.how: Rally crosscourt. On any short ball, glance at your partner: if they're still getting back to the middle, go down the line; if they've moved across early, go crosscourt behind them.

lesson.cue: Where are they? Then where does it go.

steps.name: They're still recovering
steps.sit: Their crosscourt lands short. You step in, set, and they're still getting back to the middle.
steps.payoff: Down the line, they're stretched and you're set early for the next ball.
steps.principle: Change direction when they're still on their way back.
steps.why: Down the line stretches them (2.7 m/s to get there), so all they have is a safe ball, and you're set early. It lands 8 in 10. Crosscourt and the middle are safer, but go straight to them. The flat crosscourt stretches them most, but only 5 in 10 land.
steps.take: Short, and they're recovering? Down the line.

lines.A: Safe, but they're set. Back in the rally.
lines.B: Lands every time, but it's right to them.
lines.C: Right: they're stretched, and you're set early.
lines.D: Stretches them most, but only 5 in 10 land.

steps.name: They're covering the line
steps.sit: Same short ball. This time they've started moving toward the line before you hit.
steps.payoff: Crosscourt goes behind them. At full stretch, all they have is a defensive ball.
steps.principle: If they're covering the line, go crosscourt.
steps.why: They're already moving to the line, so the line goes to them. Crosscourt goes behind them: they reach it at full stretch and can only defend, and it lands 9 in 10. The flat crosscourt wins outright here, but only 5 in 10 land.
steps.take: They're covering the line? Crosscourt, behind them.

lines.A: Straight to where they're going. Back in the rally.
lines.C: A winner this time, but only 5 in 10 land.
lines.D: Right: behind them. All they have is a defensive ball.

steps.name: The same on your backhand
steps.sit: Their crosscourt backhand lands short to your backhand. They're still on their way back to the middle.
steps.payoff: Down the line, they're stretched again. You're set for the next ball.
steps.principle: Same rule on the backhand: line while they're still recovering.
steps.why: Down the line goes away from where they're heading, so they're stretched, and it lands 9 in 10. Crosscourt lands every time, but they're set. The middle goes right to them and leaves you only just in time.
steps.take: Backhand too: line while they're recovering.

lines.A: Right at them. You're only just in time.
lines.B: Right: they're still on the way back. Stretched.
lines.C: Lands every time, but they're set.
